hero.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
hero.body:
Federal authorities arrested a former CIA official after discovering 303 gold bars worth approximately $40 million in his home. The FBI made the arrest after conducting a search of the residence.

Prosecutors accused the former officer of stealing the gold bars from the government during his time at the agency. The arrest followed an investigation into the theft of the valuable assets from CIA holdings.

The former official allegedly lied about his credentials during his employment with the intelligence agency. Authorities have not disclosed the duration of the theft or how long the gold bars were stored at the residence before their discovery.

The case represents one of the largest alleged thefts by a government employee in recent years. The gold bars were seized by federal agents during the search operation that led to the arrest.

The FBI conducted the investigation that resulted in the charges against the former CIA officer. The criminal complaint details allegations of both the theft and false statements made regarding his qualifications for the position.

Federal prosecutors are handling the case, which involves charges related to the theft of government property valued at tens of millions of dollars. The former officer faces multiple charges stemming from the alleged theft and deception during his tenure at the CIA.

The investigation into how the theft occurred over time and whether other individuals were involved continues. Authorities have not released the name of the accused or specific details about when the alleged theft began.

The discovery of such a large quantity of gold bars in a private residence marked a significant development in the case. The 303 bars represent a substantial portion of valuable government assets that went missing from CIA custody.

cards.headline: US and Iran reach tentative deal to extend ceasefire and begin nuclear talks
cards.body:
US and Iranian negotiators have reached a tentative agreement on a framework deal to extend their ceasefire and establish talks about Iran's nuclear program, according to multiple reports. The agreement awaits final approval from President Trump before it can take effect.

The proposed 60-day ceasefire extension would involve several key provisions. Iran would clear mines it deployed in the Strait of Hormuz and agree not to impose tolls on ships passing through the waterway. In return, the US would lift its blockade on Iranian ports that has been in effect since April 13. During this period, the strait would be reopened and Iran could freely sell oil on international markets.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the deal could achieve "a completely open" Strait of Hormuz "without tolls" if successful. However, Iranian media reported that the strait would remain under Iranian control.

The framework also includes unfreezing some Iranian assets held in banks outside Iran and halting hostilities on all fronts, including between Israel and Lebanon.

The tentative deal comes after recent military exchanges tested the fragile ceasefire. The US military reported that Iran launched a ballistic missile toward Kuwait, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed to have targeted an unspecified US base in retaliation for earlier American strikes.

Nuclear negotiations would occur during the ceasefire extension, though significant disagreements remain about what that involves. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Tehran had not agreed to hand over its stockpile of highly enriched uranium and that Iran's nuclear issue was not part of the preliminary agreement with the US. This contradicted earlier reporting that Iran had expressed willingness to give up the stockpile.

The agreement does not appear to address Iran's ballistic missile program or Iran's support for regional allies including Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen.

Oil markets reacted positively to news of the potential agreement, with prices pulling back on reports of the ceasefire extension. The agreement represents a potential de-escalation in tensions that have threatened to derail negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

The three-month war preceding the current ceasefire had raised concerns about regional stability and global energy markets. Neither government has released comprehensive details about the agreement's terms or the timeline for nuclear negotiations.

Trump has not yet publicly commented on the tentative deal or indicated when he might make a decision. Officials from both sides have continued working to reach agreement even as military hostilities persisted.

cards.headline: US military reports Iran launched ballistic missile toward Kuwait amid ceasefire
cards.teaser: The US military said Iran launched a ballistic missile toward Kuwait as military exchanges threatened ongoing negotiations.
cards.body:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a ballistic missile targeting a US base in retaliation for earlier American strikes, according to US military reports. The attack occurred despite an ongoing three-month ceasefire between the two countries.

The missile exchange marks a escalation in hostilities, though neither side appears willing to return to full-scale conflict. US and Iranian negotiators have reached a tentative agreement to extend the ceasefire and begin nuclear talks, pending final approval from US officials.

cards.headline: US Inflation Rises as Iran War Pushes Up Prices
cards.body:
US inflation has accelerated to its fastest pace in nearly three years, driven largely by higher energy prices stemming from the ongoing conflict with Iran. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.8 percent from a year earlier in April, exceeding the Federal Reserve's target and squeezing American households.

The inflation report marks the first reading under new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh. According to Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, the situation reflects mounting financial pressure on consumers. "Inflation is at a three-year high and personal savings has cratered to one of the lowest levels in the past 20 years. Many Americans are spending more than the income they have coming in. This is not sustainable, especially for lower-income and middle-class households."

The elevated inflation comes as US economic growth has also disappointed. GDP expanded at an annual rate of 1.6 percent at the start of the year, down from an initially estimated 2 percent. Combined with rising prices, this slowdown has eroded Americans' purchasing power and real incomes.

Energy prices have been particularly sensitive to developments in the Iran situation. The conflict has contributed to sustained pressure on oil markets, with costs flowing through to broader consumer expenses across the economy. Oil prices have fluctuated sharply based on diplomatic developments, falling back toward $94.50 per barrel after reports emerged of potential progress in ceasefire negotiations.

According to reports on Thursday, US and Iranian negotiators have reached an agreement on a 60-day memorandum of understanding to extend their ceasefire and launch negotiations on Iran's nuclear program. However, the deal remains subject to approval from President Donald Trump. News of the potential agreement temporarily boosted stock markets and eased oil prices, though uncertainty persists about final implementation.

Even if the war were to end, relief at the pump may not come quickly. Pre-war US gas prices averaged around $3 per gallon nationally, a level unlikely to return this year even with a lasting peace agreement. Energy analysts warn that fuel prices may remain elevated for an extended period regardless of diplomatic breakthroughs.

Warsh now faces the challenge of addressing inflation that exceeds the Federal Reserve's targets while navigating ongoing geopolitical tensions. The central bank must weigh its policy options carefully, balancing the need to control inflation against the uncertainty created by the conflict and potential ceasefire negotiations.

The inflation data demonstrates how international military conflicts transmit through global markets to affect domestic economic conditions. As the Fed contemplates its next moves, policymakers will be monitoring whether energy prices stabilize following any potential resolution to the Iran conflict.

cards.headline: Sweden to provide Ukraine with 16 Gripen fighter jets, opens deal for 22 more
cards.teaser: Sweden agreed to hand over 16 Gripen jets armed with long-range missiles and opened negotiations for Ukraine to purchase up to 22 additional aircraft.
cards.body:
Sweden will provide Ukraine with 16 Gripen fighter jets equipped with missiles capable of striking targets 200 kilometers away. The country also opened a deal for Ukraine to acquire up to 22 more jets, with some reports indicating Ukraine will purchase 20 new Gripen aircraft.

The agreement includes both donated older model jets to be delivered sooner and newly manufactured aircraft for purchase. Ukrainian President Zelenskiy traveled to Sweden for the announcement of the fighter jet deal, according to sources familiar with the visit.

cards.headline: Israel conducts strike on Lebanese capital Beirut
cards.teaser: Israel hit Beirut in what it described as a targeted strike, escalating attacks on the Lebanese capital that had largely been spared until now.
cards.body:
Israel carried out a strike on Beirut, marking an escalation in attacks on the Lebanese capital. The city had largely been spared despite ongoing tensions between Israel and Hezbollah over the ceasefire agreement reached last month.

Both Israel and Hezbollah have accused each other of violating the ceasefire terms. The strike represents a shift in the conflict, as military operations have traditionally focused on other areas of Lebanon rather than the capital itself.

cards.headline: Supreme Court sides with Mississippi death row inmate in racial bias case
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled in favor of a Black man on death row who alleged racial bias in jury selection.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in favor of Terry Pitchford, a Black man on death row in Mississippi convicted of capital murder. Pitchford argued that racial bias affected his jury's composition, claiming that Black jurors were excluded during jury selection in violation of his constitutional rights.

The decision represents a significant win for Pitchford in his challenge to the jury that convicted him.

cards.headline: At least 16 students killed in Kenya school fire
cards.teaser: A fire at a Kenyan school left at least 16 pupils dead, with parents still waiting for news of their children hours after the blaze.
cards.body:
At least 16 students died in a fire that broke out just after midnight at Utumishi girls academy in Gilgil, Nakuru county, located about 76 miles northwest of Nairobi. The blaze tore through a dormitory at the school.

Hours after the fire, several parents were still waiting for news of their children. The incident adds to a pattern of deadly school fires in Kenya, raising concerns about building safety and emergency preparedness at educational institutions.

cards.headline: Israeli strike on Gaza kills at least five children, targets Hamas commander
cards.teaser: A strike in Gaza City killed at least five children and appears to have targeted a Hamas commander, according to local hospitals.
cards.body:
An Israeli strike on Gaza City killed at least five children in a residential building, according to hospitals in the area. The attack appeared to target a Hamas commander.

Hamas said Mohammed Odeh, the head of its military wing, was killed in the strike along with his wife and two children. Israel's operation has been focused on eliminating Hamas leadership in Gaza.

cards.headline: Three injured in stabbing at Swiss train station, suspect arrested
cards.teaser: A 31-year-old Swiss man was arrested after three people were injured in a stabbing at a train station in Switzerland.
cards.body:
Three people were injured in a stabbing attack at a Swiss train station. Police arrested a 31-year-old Swiss man in connection with the incident.

Photographs from the scene captured sections of the station surrounded by police cordons as authorities investigated the attack.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer will not run for president in 2028
cards.teaser: Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not seek the presidency in 2028.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer said she does not plan to run for president in 2028. The announcement removes a prominent Democrat from early speculation about the next presidential race.

Whitmer has served as Michigan's governor and was previously considered a potential candidate for national office. Her decision not to pursue the presidency leaves the field open for other Democratic contenders in the next election cycle.

cards.headline: Federal judge declines to block Trump executive order on mail-in voting
cards.teaser: A federal judge in Washington declined to block an executive order limiting mail-in voting.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C., has refused to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. Democrats had challenged the order in court seeking an immediate injunction to prevent its implementation.

The decision allows the executive order to move forward while legal challenges continue in court. Another judge may rule on the matter soon.

cards.headline: Iran says it targeted American base after fresh US strikes
cards.teaser: Iran reported targeting an American military base following new US strikes in the region.
cards.body:
Iran said it targeted an American base in response to recent US strikes. The military exchange marks an escalation during what both sides describe as a fragile ceasefire meant to allow diplomatic efforts.

The hostilities occur as negotiations continue over a three-month conflict between the two nations. Despite the latest strikes, neither side appears eager to return to full-scale war, suggesting room for continued diplomatic efforts.

cards.headline: Hezbollah adopts fiber-optic drones in strikes against Israel
cards.teaser: Hezbollah has made fiber-optic drones its primary weapon in attacks on Israeli targets.
cards.body:
Fiber-optic drones have become the main weapon used by Hezbollah against Israeli soldiers and civilians. The militant group adopted the technology after observing its use in Ukraine.

The drones rely on fiber-optic connections rather than radio signals, making them harder to detect and jam. Hezbollah has shifted its tactics to focus on this technology in its ongoing conflict with Israel.

cards.headline: Man dies after escaping vehicle on way to court, struck by train
cards.teaser: A man was killed by a train after fleeing a vehicle while being transported to court.
cards.body:
A man died after escaping from a vehicle during transport to court and being struck by a train. The incident occurred in Hertfordshire and has been referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct.

Hertfordshire Police reported the death and initiated the referral process for an independent investigation. The circumstances surrounding how the man escaped from the vehicle are part of the ongoing inquiry.

cards.headline: Tilman Fertitta to Acquire Caesars Entertainment for $18 Billion
cards.teaser: The Houston Rockets owner and hospitality executive is buying the casino company in one of the largest gaming industry deals in years.
cards.body:
Tilman Fertitta's Fertitta Entertainment agreed to acquire Caesars Entertainment in an $18 billion transaction, expanding his leisure and hospitality holdings. The deal values Caesars at $17.6 billion according to some reports, with the purchase price at $5.7 billion in others, reflecting different measures of the transaction.

The combined company will control four Atlantic City casinos following the acquisition. Fertitta, who owns the Houston Rockets and runs a hospitality empire, is a Trump ally and has been expanding his presence in the gaming and entertainment sectors. The transaction represents one of the largest consolidations in the casino industry.

cards.headline: Google Engineer Charged with Using Company Data for $1 Million in Prediction Market Bets
cards.teaser: An information security engineer at Google faces charges for allegedly using confidential search data to place winning bets on Polymarket.
cards.body:
A Google software engineer has been charged with using insider information to profit from bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. Michele Spagnuolo, 36, allegedly leveraged confidential data about Google's most-searched terms to place wagers and earned $1.2 million in profits. According to the complaint unsealed by the US Department of Justice, he risked over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign.

The case marks another prosecution for insider trading in the emerging prediction market space. Spagnuolo's arrest follows a similar charge against a US Army soldier accused of using classified information to place bets on Polymarket regarding military action in Venezuela.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Rise on Report of Progress in Iran Negotiations
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq moved toward record closes following reports that negotiators reached a deal to extend the Iran ceasefire.
cards.body:
US stock markets rose on Thursday following reports of an extended ceasefire agreement with Iran, subject to President Trump's approval. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq climbed on optimism surrounding the potential deal, with the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq tracking toward record closing levels. Bond yields eased despite higher PCE inflation data, as investors focused on diplomatic progress.

Oil prices initially moved higher but later fell after the breakthrough report. Global oil prices declined on Thursday following the ceasefire announcement.

cards.headline: EU Fines Temu $200 Million for Allowing Sale of Illegal Products
cards.teaser: The European Commission penalized the Chinese-owned online retailer for failing to address risks from unsafe baby toys and faulty chargers on its platform.
cards.body:
The European Commission has fined Temu €200 million for failing to prevent illegal and dangerous products from being sold on its platform. A 19-month investigation found that consumers were very likely to encounter unsafe items, including hazardous baby toys and faulty electronics.

The penalty reflects Temu's inadequate risk management in its marketplace operations. The Chinese-owned retailer did not take sufficient measures to stop dangerous products from being listed and sold to European consumers, violating EU consumer protection standards.

cards.headline: Trump Refiles $10 Billion Defamation Suit Against Wall Street Journal
cards.teaser: The lawsuit, which centers on an article about a birthday note to Jeffrey Epstein, returns to court after an earlier version was dismissed.
cards.body:
Former President Donald Trump's legal team has refiled a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over a story alleging he sent a letter to Jeffrey Epstein in 2003. A Florida judge had dismissed the original case last month, prompting Trump to bring the action back to court with modifications.

The lawsuit claims the newspaper's reporting tarnished Trump's reputation by describing the correspondence as bearing his signature. The case represents a high-profile legal clash between Trump and Rupert Murdoch, who owns the Wall Street Journal.

cards.headline: Bari Weiss Appoints Nick Bilton to Lead CBS's 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The tech journalist and filmmaker will take over the program as CBS's editor in chief reshapes the news division, including firing correspondent Cecilia Vega.
cards.body:
Nick Bilton, a tech journalist and filmmaker, has been appointed to lead CBS's 60 Minutes under editor in chief Bari Weiss. Bilton said he plans to bring new voices to the long-running news program.

The appointment is part of a broader restructuring at CBS News. The leadership changes have included staff transitions, with correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi's contract not being renewed for the show's upcoming 59th season.

hero.headline: U.S. says troops were targeted with location data as lawmaker calls ad industry a national security threat
hero.body:
U.S. military personnel have been identified and tracked using location information purchased from the advertising technology industry, federal officials have confirmed. The disclosure has prompted lawmakers to escalate calls for treating the adtech sector as a national security threat.

The revelation underscores mounting congressional anxiety about how location data harvested from smartphones and mobile applications can be bought and weaponized to monitor the movements of military personnel and other sensitive populations.

The advertising technology industry routinely collects precise location information from mobile apps and websites, then packages and sells this data to brokers who distribute it widely. This information can reveal movement patterns and identify individuals based on their homes, workplaces, and travel routes. Security experts have long flagged the potential for foreign adversaries to exploit such data for harmful purposes.

The targeting of U.S. troops through commercially purchased location information demonstrates that these theoretical dangers have materialized into concrete security risks. Military installations and service members face particular vulnerability because their movements can expose sensitive operational details.

The industry has previously contended that its data collection practices are sufficiently anonymized to pose minimal privacy concerns. However, researchers have consistently shown that location data enables individual identification even when names and obvious identifiers are removed. The geographic patterns of people's daily lives, particularly visits to residences and offices, frequently provide sufficient detail to determine identity.

This incident has energized legislative momentum to regulate data brokers and constrain the sale of Americans' location information. Recent congressional proposals would prohibit data brokers from selling sensitive location data, particularly information that could track military personnel, intelligence officials, or other government employees.

One prominent privacy advocate stated it was time to begin "treating the adtech industry as a national security threat," reflecting the seriousness with which lawmakers now view the issue.

The Pentagon has implemented limited protective measures, including issuing guidance to service members about applications that collect location data. However, officials acknowledge that voluntary approaches may prove inadequate if the underlying data marketplace continues operating without meaningful restrictions.

The incident parallels recent enforcement actions against companies that mishandle consumer data. In a separate case, General Motors agreed to pay 12.75 million dollars to resolve claims it sold hundreds of thousands of Californians' location and driving information to data brokers without consent. The company had collected the data through its OnStar subscription service while generating approximately 20 million dollars from these sales between 2020 and 2024.

The GM settlement included a five-year prohibition on selling consumer data to data brokers, demonstrating regulators' willingness to impose strict penalties for unauthorized data sales.

cards.headline: Waymo launches Chinese-made Ojai minivan robotaxi, now accepting riders
cards.teaser: The autonomous vehicle company begins service with a new robotaxi after years of development and testing.
cards.body:
Waymo has begun accepting passengers in its new Ojai robotaxi, a Chinese-manufactured minivan based on the Zeekr RT. The company will initially offer free rides to select passengers in San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix before gradually expanding to additional riders and cities.

The launch follows months of testing and comes during a challenging period for the autonomous vehicle company. Waymo designed the Ojai specifically for robotaxi operations as it works toward profitability in its ride-hailing business.

cards.headline: Musk reframes Anthropic compute deal as short-term despite SpaceX filing showing 2029 payments
cards.teaser: Elon Musk publicly described the compute agreement as cancellable, contradicting details in SpaceX's regulatory filing.
cards.body:
Elon Musk is publicly characterizing xAI's compute deal with Anthropic as short-term and potentially cancellable. This framing contrasts with SpaceX's S-1 regulatory filing, which indicates payments extending through May 2029.

The disagreement highlights differing interpretations of the agreement's terms. Musk's public statements suggest flexibility to end the arrangement, while SpaceX's official filing presents it as a multi-year commitment with defined payment obligations.

cards.headline: Rivian faces federal investigation over rear suspension failures causing loss of vehicle control
cards.teaser: At least two owners lost control after a suspension component broke, both following prior service work.
cards.body:
Federal regulators have launched an investigation into Rivian following rear suspension failures on R1 models. At least two vehicle owners experienced loss of control after a critical suspension component broke.

Both incidents involved vehicles that had undergone prior service. The investigation will determine whether a pattern exists in the rear suspension failures and assess whether the previous service work played a role in the component breakdowns.

cards.headline: Steam Deck sells out in North America following price increase exceeding 40 percent
cards.teaser: Valve's handheld gaming device sold out despite a price hike driven by component costs.
cards.body:
The Steam Deck has sold out across North America following price increases exceeding 40 percent. Valve attributed the price hike to rising component costs, noting that the device itself remained unchanged.

The quick sellout demonstrates sustained consumer interest in the handheld gaming platform despite the substantial price increase. The device had previously been unavailable for an extended period before returning to the market at the higher price point.

cards.headline: Sesame launches iOS app bringing conversational AI from Oculus founders to public
cards.teaser: The startup's new app offers AI agents designed to feel more like talking to a person than using traditional chatbots.
cards.body: Sesame, founded by the creators of Oculus, has released its iOS app to bring conversational AI technology to a broader audience. The app features AI agents designed to enable more natural interactions than traditional chatbots, allowing users to engage in back-and-forth conversations that feel closer to talking with another person rather than using a standard bot interface.

cards.headline: Apple's iOS 27 redesign previewed with new Siri app and AI features
cards.teaser: New renders show Apple's planned overhaul including a standalone Siri application and redesigned interface.
cards.body:
Leaked renders of iOS 27 reveal Apple's planned overhaul of Siri, featuring a standalone app with a chat interface comparable to ChatGPT. The redesign represents a significant shift in how users will interact with Apple's voice assistant, moving toward a more conversational AI experience.

The preview also shows updates to other iOS features, including changes to the Camera app, Dynamic Island interface, and AirPods settings menu. These renders, based on information obtained by Bloomberg and industry sources, offer the first detailed look at Apple's broader artificial intelligence strategy for the upcoming operating system.

hero.headline: Racer Dies in Isle of Man TT Qualifying Crash
hero.body:
The Isle of Man TT is an annual motorcycle racing event held on public roads on the Isle of Man. The race is known for its challenging course and high speeds.

Ingham's death occurred during a qualifying session ahead of the main race events. Qualifying sessions allow competitors to set lap times that determine their starting positions in the races.

The Isle of Man TT has a long history dating back over a century. The event attracts riders from around the world who compete on a 37.73-mile course that winds through villages and countryside on the island.

The race has seen numerous fatalities over its history due to the demanding nature of the course, which features tight corners, elevation changes, and speeds that can exceed 200 miles per hour on certain sections.

Wednesday's qualifying session was part of the preparations for the 2026 edition of the event. Riders use qualifying sessions to familiarize themselves with track conditions and push for optimal lap times.

Ingham was competing as one of many riders attempting to qualify for the main race events scheduled to take place later in the week. The TT typically spans multiple days with different race categories and distances.

Race organizers have not released additional details about the circumstances of the crash. The qualifying session in which Ingham was participating continued to be part of the scheduled preparations for the upcoming races.

cards.headline: Top-Ranked Jannik Sinner Loses at French Open
cards.teaser: World number one tennis player Jannik Sinner was eliminated from the French Open in the second round.
cards.body:
World No. 1 Jannik Sinner's bid for a first French Open title has ended after a second-round defeat to Juan Manuel Cerundolo in a five-set match. The injury-hampered loss marks another year without capturing the only Grand Slam tournament missing from his career resume.

The upset exit came during an exceptionally hot French Open, with Sinner unable to overcome both his physical struggles and Cerundolo's challenge on the court.

cards.headline: Japanese Slugger Munetaka Murakami Reaches 20 Home Runs
cards.teaser: Munetaka Murakami hit his 20th home run of the season in 55 games, placing him among the fastest to reach that mark in baseball history.
cards.body:
Munetaka Murakami, who plays for an MLB team, reached the 20-home run milestone through 55 games this season. The achievement ranks among the fastest starts in Major League Baseball history. Murakami, referred to as the Japanese Babe Ruth, also recorded his first stolen base of the season.

Murakami hit a game-tying home run in the eighth inning during a game against the Minnesota Twins. His team, the White Sox, eventually lost in extra innings. Murakami leads the American League in home runs and has accomplished something not seen in MLB since 1901.

cards.headline: Ronda Rousey Says She Would Win Holly Holm Rematch
cards.teaser: Former UFC fighter Ronda Rousey responded to rematch talk with Holly Holm, saying she would win but maintaining she is retired.
cards.body:
Ronda Rousey responded to Holly Holm's rematch speculation by claiming she would decisively beat her in a potential fight. Despite the confident assertion, Rousey emphasized that she remains retired from competition and has no plans to return to active fighting.

Holm had expressed skepticism about whether Rousey would be willing to face her again following Rousey's recent victory over Gina Carano. The two fighters previously competed in a UFC bout that resulted in Holm defeating Rousey and ending her undefeated record.

cards.headline: Vikings Quarterbacks Murray and McCarthy Address Competition
cards.teaser: Minnesota Vikings quarterbacks Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy discussed their relationship as they compete for the starting position.
cards.body:
Kyler Murray said his relationship with J.J. McCarthy has been great as the two quarterbacks compete for the Vikings starting job. Murray and McCarthy both described themselves as competitors while addressing the quarterback battle.

McCarthy stated there is no awkwardness between him and Murray regarding the competition. During organized team activities, both quarterbacks were observed distributing footballs as the team refined its techniques. Murray and McCarthy gave different answers when asked about their relationship during the competition.

cards.headline: Patriots and Eagles Not Close on A.J. Brown Trade
cards.teaser: The New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles remain far apart in negotiations for wide receiver A.J. Brown.
cards.body:
The Patriots and Eagles are not particularly close to reaching an agreement on a trade for A.J. Brown, according to reports. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts described his relationship with Brown as really good despite the trade speculation.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the team wants to strengthen the roster wherever possible when asked about adding a wide receiver. An analysis suggested the Eagles and Brown are heading toward a separation, with discussion of what comes next for both parties.

cards.headline: Anthony Gordon's Form Raises Questions for Barcelona and Rashford
cards.teaser: Anthony Gordon's performance in European competition has drawn attention ahead of potential Barcelona interest.
cards.body:
Anthony Gordon has impressed in European competition, delivering strong goal returns alongside his distinctive speed, aggression and work ethic. José Mourinho publicly praised the England winger after Newcastle's 3-0 Champions League victory over Benfica, with the Benfica manager telling Gordon "you are too much" following a performance in which he scored and created a goal.

Barcelona are investing £70m to secure Gordon's services, recognizing his proven Champions League pedigree. His attributes and recent form have positioned him as one of the standout wingers in European football, explaining the club's significant commitment to the transfer.

hero.headline: CBS News Removes 60 Minutes Executive Producer and Two Correspondents
hero.body:
CBS News has removed multiple senior figures from 60 Minutes, including executive producer Tanya Simon, correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega, and senior executive producer Draggan Mihailoivich. Nick Bilton, a former technology columnist, will lead the newsmagazine going forward. The changes were made by CBS News editor in chief Bari Weiss.

The departures mark a significant restructuring at 60 Minutes, the most-watched newsmagazine program on television. Alfonsi has publicly disputed the circumstances of her exit, stating that CBS News declined to renew her contract after she refused to compromise on factually accurate reporting.

Alfonsi's contract expired after nearly two decades at CBS News, including more than a decade at 60 Minutes. In a statement, she accused the network of penalizing her for her editorial stance. "This was not a routine corporate transition; it was a deliberate choice to penalize a journalist for refusing to sanitize factually accurate reporting, and it sends a chilling message to the entire newsroom," Alfonsi wrote.

The tension between Alfonsi and network leadership intensified after CBS News shelved a segment she reported on a prison in El Salvador. Alfonsi has said the decision by Weiss was made for "political" reasons. She previously spoke publicly about what she described as "the spread of corporate meddling and editorial fear" at CBS News.

In her statement, Alfonsi criticized the network's direction more broadly. She argued that CBS management is "choosing access journalism over accountability and protecting power rather than scrutinizing it." She expressed concern about the removal of the wall between editorial independence and corporate interests at the network.

Alfonsi noted that her reporting had not appeared on the final three episodes of the show's 58th season, which ended in May. She called on her colleagues to maintain journalistic standards despite these changes.

The shake-up also affects veteran correspondent Anderson Cooper, who has decided to leave the program. In comments about his departure, Cooper emphasized that "the independence of 60 Minutes has been critical." He added, "I hope 60 Minutes remains 60 Minutes," suggesting concern about the show's future direction and potential editorial shifts.

Bilton brings a background in technology journalism to his new role overseeing 60 Minutes. He will handle editorial direction and production for the program as it enters its 59th season in the fall.

The personnel changes affect multiple levels of the show's operations, from senior production positions to on-air talent. The restructuring comes as industry insiders worry about potential impacts on the program's standing as a leading television news broadcast.

cards.headline: Zac Efron to Star in HBO and A24 Series Based on Angel Heart Novel
cards.teaser: Zac Efron will star in and executive produce a one-hour drama series for HBO and A24 based on the 1978 horror novel Falling Angel.
cards.body:
The series is written and executive produced by Zach Baylin, creator of Black Rabbit. The project adapts the novel Falling Angel, which was previously made into the 1987 film Angel Heart starring Mickey Rourke and Robert De Niro.

Effron will take on both acting and producing duties for the hour-long drama. HBO and A24 are co-producing the series, bringing together the premium cable network and the independent studio known for prestige film and television projects.

cards.headline: Chrissy Metz to Make Broadway Debut in Jukebox Musical
cards.teaser: Chrissy Metz will make her first Broadway appearance in the musical & Juliet starting in June.
cards.body:
Metz will join the cast as the character Anglique for a limited run from June 18 through Sept. 13. The actress is known for playing Kate Pearson on the NBC television series This Is Us.

Her character on This Is Us had professional singing ambitions, which required Metz to perform vocally on the show. She will now bring those skills to the Broadway stage in the jukebox musical, which reimagines the story of Juliet with contemporary pop songs.

cards.headline: Disney+ to Release Three New Simpsons Episodes This Summer
cards.teaser: The Simpsons will premiere three original episodes exclusively on Disney+ between June and July.
cards.body:
The first release will be a double episode titled Extreme Makeover: Homer Edition, launching June 17 on Disney+. Two additional full-length episodes will follow: Simpsley on July 3 and Yellow on an unspecified date.

Guest stars for the summer episodes include musician Laufey and actress Betty Gilpin. The releases continue The Simpsons' strategy of creating exclusive content for the Disney+ streaming platform in addition to its regular broadcast schedule.

cards.headline: Karen Gillan Joins Shrinking for Fourth Season
cards.teaser: Karen Gillan has been cast in a recurring role for the fourth season of the Apple TV+ series Shrinking.
cards.body:
Karen Gillan has been cast in a recurring role for Shrinking's fourth season. The Apple TV+ dramedy was renewed for another season earlier this year, ahead of the third season's premiere on the streaming service.

Gillan will join the show's existing cast, which includes Jason Segel, Harrison Ford, Christa Miller, Jessica Williams, Luke Tennie, Michael Urie, and Lukita Maxwell. Shrinking follows a therapist who begins disregarding professional boundaries by speaking his mind directly to his clients.

cards.headline: Media Access Awards Rebrands as Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards
cards.teaser: The Media Access Awards, which recognize disability representation in film and television, have been renamed the Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards.
cards.body:
The awards will now be known as the Darcys. Easterseals Disability Services and disability community leaders are leading the rebranding effort, with Film Independent serving as co-producer.

Norman Lear originally founded the awards in 1979. The program honors authentic filmmaking and representation of people with disabilities in media. The rebrand aims to emphasize both arts and culture in recognizing disability representation across entertainment.

cards.headline: Fox Creator Studios Partners With Tom Segura's YMH Studios
cards.teaser: Fox Creator Studios has set a production deal with comedian Tom Segura's YMH Studios to develop content for digital and direct-to-consumer channels.
cards.body:
The agreement calls for Fox Creator Studios and YMH to jointly develop and finance projects that will be released through YMH's established digital and podcast platforms. The content will appear on Segura's existing channels rather than traditional broadcast.

Segura operates YMH Studios as a digital content production company focused on comedy and podcasting. The partnership with Fox Creator Studios will expand the studio's production capacity while keeping distribution on Segura's owned platforms.

hero.headline: US and Iran reach tentative agreement to extend ceasefire, reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for an additional 60 days and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.S. sources. The arrangement still requires approval from President Trump before it takes effect.

The two countries have agreed to a 60-day memorandum of understanding that would prolong the current ceasefire beyond its scheduled expiration on April 22. The White House has confirmed the tentative framework following indirect negotiations mediated by Pakistan's military leadership.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said the administration feels "good about the prospects of a deal," though she emphasized that nothing is official until confirmed by the White House. She noted that a second round of negotiations would likely be held in Islamabad.

Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, traveled to Tehran to convey messages from Washington and help arrange further ceasefire talks. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif simultaneously embarked on a four-day diplomatic tour through Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey to build regional support for a peace agreement.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson said views from both sides would be discussed in detail during these visits. However, sources in Tehran indicated Iran has demanded an end to Israeli attacks on Lebanon as a precondition for additional negotiations.

The agreement addresses two critical issues: extending the ceasefire to prevent renewed conflict and reopening the strategic waterway that handles global oil shipments.

Trump has made aggressive statements regarding the Strait of Hormuz. During a cabinet meeting, he threatened to "blow up" Oman if the country failed to "behave," referencing reports that Iran and Oman had discussed jointly charging a toll for ships passing through the waterway.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reinforced this position, stating that "the United States Government will not tolerate any effort to impose a tolling system in the Strait of Hormuz." Bessent also warned of escalating financial pressure on Iran, including secondary sanctions against countries and companies purchasing Iranian oil or holding Iranian funds.

The U.S. military has already implemented a naval blockade of Iranian ports, with American warships turning back nine ships that attempted to cross the strait, including a Chinese-owned tanker under U.S. sanctions.

Iran's military leadership has responded to the blockade, with a senior commander warning that Iran could halt trade in the Gulf region if the U.S. did not lift its port restrictions.

Despite the tentative agreement, Trump has not yet indicated whether he will approve the arrangement. The agreement represents a potential diplomatic shift after months of heightened regional tensions, though officials describe the current ceasefire as fragile. The 60-day timeframe would provide both sides an opportunity to negotiate longer-term solutions.

cards.headline: Trump administration pushes Bureau of Engraving to create $250 bill with president's image
cards.teaser: Trump administration officials pushed the agency that prints U.S. currency to design a $250 bill featuring President Trump, according to a new report.
cards.body:
The Bureau of Engraving and Printing was pushed by Trump administration officials to create a $250 bill, The Washington Post reported. The bureau is the government agency responsible for printing U.S. currency.

Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton criticized the reported effort in a public statement. The push for a new denomination featuring the sitting president comes as the administration pursues various initiatives ahead of the midterm elections.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent to brief press after Trump Accounts app launches
cards.teaser: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will lead the White House press briefing hours after the new investment app for Trump Accounts went live.
cards.body:
The Trump Accounts app launched Thursday, enabling Americans to access investment accounts created under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The administration has highlighted the accounts as an economic achievement.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is leading a White House press briefing Thursday afternoon following the app's launch. Earlier that morning, Bessent issued a warning to Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz, stating the U.S. would not tolerate any tolling system in the waterway.

cards.headline: Trump refiled defamation lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein coverage
cards.teaser: President Trump refiled a defamation suit against the Wall Street Journal over a 2025 report about a letter to Jeffrey Epstein bearing his signature.
cards.body:
Trump's legal team has refiled a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal after a Florida judge dismissed the case last month. The suit challenges the newspaper's 2025 report describing a "bawdy" letter Trump allegedly sent to Jeffrey Epstein in 2003 as bearing his signature.

The refiled case pits the president against Rupert Murdoch, who owns the Wall Street Journal. Trump claims the newspaper's coverage damaged his reputation through its reporting on the Epstein-related correspondence.

cards.headline: Transportation Secretary announces $465 million for Union Station repairs
cards.teaser: The Trump administration will provide more than $400 million to upgrade Washington Union Station after taking federal control of the facility last year.
cards.body:
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced a $465 million grant for Union Station repairs. The administration restored federal control of the Washington facility last year.

Duffy said the funding supports President Trump's call to make the nation's capital beautiful and great again. The grant will pay for upgrades to the historic transportation hub, which serves as a major transit point in Washington.

cards.headline: At least $2 million paid in settlements over Charlie Kirk firing cases
cards.teaser: Employers agreed to at least $2 million in settlements after firing or penalizing workers who criticized Charlie Kirk following his death.
cards.body:
At least $2 million was paid out in settlements after employees and critics were fired or penalized over posts about Charlie Kirk. An estimated 600 individuals faced termination or punishment for criticizing the conservative political activist or downplaying his death.

The Trump administration backed the employment actions at the time. Kirk's death became the center of a debate over free speech and employer authority. The settlements demonstrate the limits employers face when regulating workers' political speech.

cards.headline: Cuba faces worsening blackouts as fuel shortages grip island
cards.teaser: Prolonged power outages are disrupting essential services in Cuba as the country struggles with limited fuel supply.
cards.body:
Cuba is experiencing a humanitarian crisis as fuel shortages cause prolonged blackouts across the island. The power outages are disrupting essential services and making basic tasks like cooking difficult or impossible for the country's nearly 11 million residents.

The fuel shortage intensified after the U.S. captured former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January, cutting off Cuba's key oil supplier. Residents have struggled to keep refrigerators running and maintain basic household functions during the extended blackouts.
